markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize **leave-self-out agreement-weighted recent-history residuals with uniform multi-negative cross-entropy**. Retain the original self-inclusive formula as a control; no improvement has been measured.

**Insights and directions.** Three starting insights remain useful. Zero initialization preserves initial SASRec scores, provided shared parameters are identical. Five-item pooling emphasizes current activity, but its original self-inclusive formula guarantees latest-item dominance: with five nonzero embeddings, latest weight is at least 0.636 and approximately 0.826 when older cosine similarities are zero. Candidate cross-entropy introduces competition, but objective and negative-count effects require separate controls.

Three related-work insights refine the proposal. CLSR motivates separating persistent and immediate interests [1]; agreement with the latest embedding alone does not establish repeated preference. gSASRec motivates objective controls [2], although Electronics’ 9.61% negative diagnostic margins do not identify an objective defect. MAN and ReZero establish precedents for similarity pooling and zero-initialized residual gates [4,5], reducing originality claims; directed graph projections remain an alternative [3].

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Intent representation | SASRec; CLSR; MAN | Leave-self-out agreement residual |
| Ranking objective | Sampled BCE; gSASRec | BCE/CE × 1/32 negatives |
| Behavioral direction | Directed transitions | Separate source/target score |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. Each dimension includes a positive and negative reason.

- **A: Revised agreement residual + CE [1,2,4,5]: 3/6/6/7/5.** Originality: controlled adaptation / established ingredients; potential: extensible / uncertain benefit; user: targets stale and broad associations / no necessity inference; model: tests weak separation / may reinforce latest-item shortcuts; difficulty: small branch / extensive controls and sampling work.
- **B: CE alone [2]: 2/6/3/8/2.** Originality: clean control / established objective; potential: transferable / bounded contribution; user: sharper competition / no explicit intent mechanism; model: targets separation / in-sample evidence; difficulty: simple loss / exclusions require care.
- **C: Directed-transition residual [3]: 5/7/6/6/5.** Originality: asymmetric fusion / known transitions; potential: task sequences / sparse counts; user: successive needs / compatibility unverified; model: alternative separation / popularity confounds; difficulty: lightweight scoring / extra artifacts.

**Selected algorithm.** A targets older/occasional interests outweighing current activity and broad associations displacing specific matches. Restricting aggregation to recent earlier inputs tests historical support for current activity without including self-similarity. It does not establish repeated preference, compatibility, satisfied needs, or causal intent. CE separately targets Electronics’ observed separation weakness.

```text
For each valid prefix ending at t:
  h = SASRec(prefix)
  J = nonpadding positions among t-4,...,t-1
  w[j] ∝ exp(-(t-j) + cosine(e[j], e[t]))
  r = LayerNorm(W * sum(w[j] * e[j])); r=0 if J empty
  z = h + tanh(a) * r; initialize a=0
  Train CE([positive, up to 32 distinct uniform negatives], temperature=1)
```

Exclude padding and complete known training positives; retain repeated targets. Use staged, preregistered objective and branch controls with matched exposure; report compute separately. Select solely by pinned macro sampled validation HR@10, reporting paired category differences and selection limitations [6–8]. Preserve four-category routing, seeds, data path, diagnostic interfaces, and predictor reconstruction. Pairwise diagnostics remain distinct from HR@10; full-catalog usefulness remains unproven.

idea.description: Revise the original agreement-weighted residual by excluding the latest input item from its own recent-history pool. For each causal prefix, pool up to four preceding input embeddings using position decay and cosine agreement with the latest input embedding, project and normalize that pool, and add it to SASRec through a zero-initialized scalar gate. Train with uniform multiple-negative sampled-candidate cross-entropy. Retain the original five-item self-inclusive formula, latest-only residual, and decay-only alternatives as controls.
idea.motivation: The proposal explicitly targets two user-facing failures: older or occasional interests receiving disproportionate influence, and broad associations displacing specific matches to current activity. A short earlier-history pool limits stale contributions, while agreement weighting tests whether recent historical support improves specificity. These are hypotheses: four earlier interactions can still represent incidental activity, and similarity does not establish repeated preference or immediate usefulness. The original formula has a specific shortcut: self-cosine equals one for a nonzero latest embedding, making its weight at least 0.636 over five valid inputs and approximately 0.826 when older similarities are zero. Removing self-inclusion eliminates that guaranteed dominance, although the latest item still controls the agreement query. Cross-entropy separately addresses Electronics’ relatively weak in-sample separation, with 9.61% negative margins and p10 near 0.054. Neither these diagnostics nor the revised mechanism establish the cause of the weakness, equipment compatibility, purchase necessity, or whether demand has already been satisfied.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use only interaction IDs initially; unavailable ratings, review text, categories, prices, stores, and simulator traits remain unused. No pretrained weights or extra datasets are required. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, original splits, all four named category routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Store all artifacts beneath the trial directory.

Define the revised branch exactly: for position t, use nonpadding positions j in [max(0,t-4),t-1]. Set logits to -(t-j)+cosine(e[j],e[t]), with cosine epsilon 1e-8 and coefficients fixed at one. These are position gaps, not elapsed time. Softmax only over eligible positions. Use raw shared item embeddings, a bias-free D-by-D projection initialized with Xavier uniform, and affine LayerNorm with epsilon 1e-5. Explicitly set the entire branch output to zero where no earlier item exists, including after normalization. Initialize scalar a=0; initialize projection normally so a can receive gradients. Add tanh(a) times the branch to original SASRec features without normalizing the combined output. Zero only padded features. The current input is permitted as the query; the next-item target is never part of the prefix.

Copy matching tensors from one canonical baseline initialization into every variant and verify equality. A shared seed alone does not guarantee equality after adding modules. Initialize added modules independently without advancing shared RNG streams. Use separate seeded streams for initialization, data ordering, negative sampling, dropout where supported, and diagnostics; preserve shared draws where feasible and document remaining differences. Record software versions and deterministic settings, acknowledging platform/version dependence.

Sample negatives before discarding user identity internally, preserving the public loader tuple (None, sequence, positive, negative). Keep complete training-history exclusion sets aligned with examples; never infer users by reverse lookup from truncated sequences. For each supervised position, exclude padding, its target, and the user's complete known training-item set. Retain repeated target occurrences as separate supervised positions. Generate up to 32 distinct uniform eligible negatives using chunked rejection sampling with duplicate rejection; switch to uniform sampling without replacement from an explicit eligible complement for dense histories. Avoid position-by-catalog weight matrices. If fewer than 32 negatives exist, use all eligible negatives and mask unused logits to negative infinity; report affected counts. Skip positions with zero eligible negatives and skip empty batches. Future validation/test interactions must never enter exclusion sets.

Compute cross-entropy on [positive_score, negative_scores] divided by temperature 1, using integer zero targets and averaging over valid supervised positions. This is sampled-candidate cross-entropy, not a claimed unbiased full-catalog softmax estimator. Apply no ad hoc LogQ correction. For BCE controls, use positive BCE plus mean negative BCE per position, then average positions, so increasing negative count does not multiply the negative loss scale. Keep optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and all otherwise unspecified baseline settings unchanged; any subsequent learning-rate or temperature tuning must be a separately logged trial.

Use a staged design within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. First run unchanged architecture under BCE/CE × 1/32 negatives, with identical exclusions, paired candidate draws across objectives, and the one-negative candidate taken from the corresponding 32-negative draw. This separates objective and candidate-count effects. Then hold the selected objective fixed and compare no branch, latest-only branch, original self-inclusive decay-only pool, original self-inclusive cosine pool, leave-self-out decay-only pool, and revised leave-self-out cosine pool. Keep projection, normalization, gate parameterization, initialization, and optimization matched across applicable branches. A similarity-shuffled weighting control is useful only if budget remains. The original baseline/objective-only/residual-only/combined comparison is recovered by also testing the revised branch under baseline BCE with one negative. Do not launch a full Cartesian search automatically.

Before any runs, declare ordered trial allocation, checkpoint evaluation cadence, tie-breaking, and exposure limits. A reproducible default is validation every 20 completed epochs through the configured limit, selecting the highest macro HR@10 and the earliest checkpoint on ties, then the earlier registered trial on cross-trial ties. Reserve budget for every category, diagnostics, and failures; charge all attempted work. If budget prevents a scheduled comparison, report it as unrun. Compare controlled ablations at matched optimizer updates and nonpadding target exposure; separately report matched-compute efficiency because equal runtime need not imply equal exposure. Record cumulative and per-trial GPU-seconds, epochs, updates, valid targets, negatives scored, all validation comparisons, and selected checkpoints.

Select using the unchanged host protocol: 200 fixed validation users per category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42, and equal-weight macro HR@10. Retain per-user binary hits if exposed by the host; do not change its evaluator to obtain them. When available, compute paired differences by independently resampling users within each category 10,000 times using an analysis-only seed 42, preserving model pairing and averaging four category deltas. Report percentile 95% intervals and category results. One changed hit is 0.5 percentage points within a category or 0.125 macro percentage points. Intervals are conditional on fixed training seed and candidate sets and do not correct repeated-validation selection optimism. If per-user hits are unavailable, report that limitation instead of inventing uncertainty estimates. Keep hidden test evaluation untouched.

Record original-pool self-weight, scalar gate magnitude, and actual residual-to-baseline feature norm ratios. Stratify descriptive results by earlier-history similarity using training-defined bins and report bin sizes; do not select checkpoints on these analyses. Full pooling must beat latest-only and decay-only controls, and cosine weighting should improve leave-self-out pooling, before attributing benefit to historical agreement. These comparisons support predictive contributions, not causal intent or disentanglement. Embedding similarity can reinforce broad associations, and complete training-history exclusions can simplify training relative to future recommendation; report both limitations.

Save architecture configuration and checkpoints and update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the exact trained branch and preserves category routing. Keep view.model bound to the actual module, item_emb shared, log2feats returning combined causal B-by-L-by-D features, and predict_score consistent with inference. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and their definitions. Preserve diagnostic state isolation; null unsupported position controls remain null unless an explicit adapter is implemented and verified. Existing pairwise margins and perturbation flips remain in-sample two-candidate measurements, not HR@10, full-catalog quality, collapse, or simulator preference evidence. No training, diagnostics, or benchmark experiments were executed for this report.
idea.pseudocode:
Create canonical baseline initialization with training seed 42.
Copy shared tensors into each registered variant; verify equality.
Initialize added projection and normalization using an independent RNG; set scalar a=0.
For each category and training batch:
    Internally retain aligned user IDs and full training-history exclusion sets.
    Sample up to K distinct uniform eligible negatives per valid position.
    Exclude padding, target, and complete known training positives.
    Preserve the public loader tuple (None, sequence, positive, negative).
    h = original_SASRec_features(sequence)
    e = item_emb(sequence)
    r = zeros_like(h)
    For each nonpadding position t:
        J = nonpadding positions in [max(0,t-4), t-1]
        If J is nonempty:
            logits[j] = -(t-j) + cosine(e[j], e[t], eps=1e-8)
            weights = softmax(logits over J)
            r[t] = LayerNorm(W(sum_j weights[j] * e[j]))
    z = h + tanh(a) * r
    For positions with a nonpadding target and at least one negative:
        scores = dot(z[t], item_emb([target, eligible_negatives])) / 1.0
        Mask unused candidate logits to negative infinity.
        position_loss = cross_entropy(scores, integer_target=0)
    If no eligible positions: skip optimizer update.
    Otherwise average position_loss and update parameters.
At preregistered checkpoints:
    Save exact configuration and weights beneath trial directory.
    Regenerate compatible working/predict.py through predictor writer.
    Obtain unchanged host macro sampled validation HR@10.
    Record every comparison and all consumed GPU-seconds.
Select highest macro HR@10; break ties by earliest checkpoint, then registered trial order.
Run staged objective and branch controls within the shared budget.
Report category deltas, available paired intervals, shortcut controls, and unrun comparisons.

originality.positive: The leave-self-out formulation and matched shortcut controls make a specific, testable adaptation of the starting proposal.
originality.negative: MAN provides similarity-weighted historical representations, ReZero provides zero-initialized scalar gates, and sampled cross-entropy is established. The exact combination warrants evaluation without claiming a new fundamental mechanism.

future_potential.positive: A small controlled branch can establish whether earlier-history agreement contributes beyond a latest-item adapter before investing in multiple timescales, timestamp gaps, or persistent-interest models.
future_potential.negative: Agreement can reinforce broad similarity and latest-item shortcuts. Gains on fixed sampled validation candidates may reflect search selection and need not improve full-catalog usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The architecture remains a short causal pooling branch using SASRec's existing embedding and scoring interfaces.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable implementation requires complete-history negative exclusions, distinct sampling, aligned internal user metadata, matched initialization and RNG controls, staged ablations, diagnostic compatibility, and predictor reconstruction.

related_work.title: [1] CLSR: Contrastive Learning for Long and Short-term Interest Modeling
contributions: Uses history-derived long-term and short-term interest proxies, contrastive supervision, and adaptive aggregation.
Motivates distinguishing persistent preference from immediate activity.
limitations: Separate branches or similarity weighting do not establish disentangled interests.
The proposed residual omits CLSR's proxy supervision and is an adaptation rather than a reproduction.

related_work.title: [2] gSASRec (2024 extended abstract)
contributions: Examines overconfidence associated with sampled binary cross-entropy in SASRec.
Proposes generalized binary cross-entropy, motivating objective-focused controls.
limitations: Does not identify the cause of the supplied Electronics diagnostic weakness.
Does not establish gains for the proposed cross-entropy variant on the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: [3] Revisiting Graph Projections for Recommendation
contributions: Combines normalized interaction graph projections with directed, inverse-distance-weighted purchase transitions.
Motivates an asymmetric transition-score alternative.
limitations: Category-based regularization cannot transfer directly because product categories are unavailable here.
Chronological associations are proxies rather than verified complementarity or compatibility labels.

related_work.title: [4] MAN (WSDM 2024)
contributions: Combines sequential backbones, including SASRec, with similarity-weighted historical-item representations.
Provides a precedent that narrows novelty claims for agreement-weighted pooling.
limitations: Its cross-domain setting differs from separate per-category training here.
Does not establish the exact proposed five-position construction or its benchmark effectiveness.

related_work.title: [5] ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Introduces zero-initialized scalar gates on residual branches.
Explains the precedent for initially preserving the backbone computation.
limitations: Zero initialization does not establish recommendation quality or prevent shortcuts.
Matching the backbone initialization and stochastic training draws requires additional controls.

related_work.title: [6] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes sampled recommendation metrics and their relationship to full-catalog evaluation.
Supports explicitly reporting the pinned metric as sampled HR@10.
limitations: Does not justify changing the host's fixed evaluator.
Sampled validation improvements cannot automatically establish full-catalog ranking improvements.

related_work.title: [7] Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides a precedent for paired bootstrap comparisons.
Motivates preserving user-level pairing when adapting resampling to category-macro recommendation differences.
limitations: The category-stratified user bootstrap is an adaptation.
Its conditional intervals exclude training-seed variability, candidate resampling variability, and adaptive search selection.

related_work.title: [8] On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit validation estimates.
Motivates preregistering trial allocation and recording every checkpoint comparison.
limitations: Logging and preregistration reduce discretion but do not eliminate selection optimism.
Ordinary paired intervals do not correct adaptive validation reuse.

related_work.title: PyTorch Reproducibility Documentation
contributions: Documents RNG control and deterministic execution settings.
Supports recording software versions and verifying matching shared initialization.
limitations: Identical seeds do not ensure reproducibility across platforms or releases.
Adding modules can alter random-number consumption unless streams and initialization are controlled.

related_work.title: Original SASRec Sampler
contributions: Excludes the user's complete training-item set when sampling negatives.
Provides a baseline exclusion contract to preserve while increasing candidate count.
limitations: Does not implement the proposed distinct 32-negative candidate construction.
The public tuple interface alone does not preserve the user metadata needed for downstream resampling.

related_work.title: nanoSASRec
contributions: Provides an implementation precedent for combining ReZero with SASRec.
limitations: An implementation precedent does not establish gains for the proposed residual.
Does not replace the required RecHarness architecture, routing, and predictor compatibility checks.
